grade.title: Conclusion
grade.subtitle: Average grades per pit, SIR, place, ore class, non-prod code or barging run — or a combination of them — for samples created in the window.
grade.averagesNote: Averages are over samples that have a Ni result.
grade.chartDescription: Highest first, up to 30 bars. Rows without any Ni result are left out of the chart; the table lists every one.

dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.intro: The lab's figures for a date window: samples, progress, cycle time and what is late.

steps.1: Pick From/To to change the window; leave them empty for the last 14 days.
steps.2: Use Filters to narrow by place, ore class, non-prod code, SIR or pit. The chips show what is applied; click a chip to remove it.
steps.3: Figures refresh by themselves every minute. "Updated" says when they were calculated; the refresh button asks again now.
steps.4: Needs attention lists samples that have been in one stage for more than 24 hours.
steps.5: TV mode opens a full-screen view for a monitor in the lab. Admin and Database can download the summary as Excel.

dashboard.tip: Figures refresh by themselves every minute. Open TV mode on the lab's monitor so everyone can see what is late.

quickSearch.title: Quick search
quickSearch.intro: Open any sample from any page.

steps.1: Press Ctrl+K (or /), or click "Search samples" at the top.
steps.2: Type a barcode, a lab code or part of a Sample ID; choose with ↑↓ and press Enter.
steps.3: A USB barcode scanner works in the same box: an exact match opens straight away.

quickSearch.tip: Plug in a USB barcode scanner and scan into the search box: an exact match opens without pressing anything else.

sampleDetail.title: A sample's page
sampleDetail.intro: Everything about one sample: where it is, its results and what happened to it.

steps.1: The timeline lists every stage scan, with corrections marked and their reason.
steps.2: The lab record shows the identity and assay results; Admin and Database also see its change history.
steps.3: Database can print a replacement label here. Admin can correct the stage, with a reason.

generate.title: Generate Barcode
generate.intro: Make new barcodes and print their QR labels. Their identity is filled in later.

steps.1: Enter how many barcodes you need, then generate. Each gets a barcode and a Lab Code, without a Sample ID yet.
steps.2: Print the labels from the preview and stick them on the bags.
steps.3: In the Sample Database, filter on "No Sample ID yet", tick the rows and use Fill in identity.

labels.title: Reprint Labels
labels.intro: Print labels again for samples that already exist.

steps.1: Search or filter the samples, then tick the ones you need.
steps.2: Choose the number of copies and columns, then print.

database.title: Sample Database
database.intro: Every lab record, with filters, export and history.

steps.1: Search by barcode, lab code or Sample ID, and filter by place, date or whether results are in.
steps.2: Database edits a record from its row; changing the identity rewrites the Sample ID automatically.
steps.3: Removed samples are kept and can be restored from the deleted view.
steps.4: Export the filtered list as Excel or CSV.
steps.5: Barcodes without a Sample ID: filter Sample ID → Not yet and press Fill in all. To correct many records at once, tick them (or select all that match) and use Fill in / change identity: the fields hold the current values — change one to set it on all of them, empty it to clear it. Drag a column heading to move it, drag its edge to resize it.

database.tip: Changing a sample's place, pit or other identity rewrites its Sample ID automatically; there is no need to edit the ID by hand.

assay.title: Enter Results
assay.intro: Put assay results in, by hand or from the instrument's spreadsheet.

steps.1: Type into the grid, or paste a block copied from Excel.
steps.2: Or upload the workbook; download the template first if you need the columns.
steps.3: Check the preview: rows are matched by Sample ID (spaces or slashes, the sack count may be left out, no ticking needed) before anything is saved.
steps.4: Sub-samples and replaced results: a Sample ID ending in a code in brackets, such as "(-20)", fills that sub-sample or creates it under its sample. A result that already has a value is only replaced after you confirm it.

assay.tip: Copy the whole block from the instrument's Excel and paste it at once; rows are matched by Lab Code or Sample ID.

grade.title: Conclusion
grade.intro: Average grades per pit, SIR, place, ore class, non-prod code or barging run, or any combination of them.

steps.1: Choose the window, then one or more groups: Pit alone, or Pit + Ore class for every combination.
steps.2: The chart shows average Ni per row; the table adds a column per group, Fe, Co, MgO, SiO₂ and the Ni range.
steps.3: Averages count only samples that have a Ni result. Download the table as Excel.

masterData.title: Master Data
masterData.intro: The codes a Sample ID is built from: place, ore class, non-prod, pit and SIR.

steps.1: Add a code with its optional description.
steps.2: A code already inside Sample IDs cannot be renamed; edit its description instead.
steps.3: Retire a code to take it out of the pickers. Delete moves its samples to a replacement code first and rewrites their Sample IDs.

masterData.tip: If a code is still inside Sample IDs, Retire is the safer choice: old samples keep reading correctly.

activity.title: Activity
activity.intro: Who did what: every stage scan, and every sign-in attempt.

steps.1: Stage activity lists scans and corrections; filter by person, stage or day.
steps.2: Sign-in audit shows each sign-in and how it was verified (face, code, password only), plus password changes and sessions ended.

mobile.title: Mobile app (scanning)
mobile.intro: Moving samples through the stages with the phone.

steps.1: Sign in with your password and face or authenticator code.
steps.2: Choose the stage, then scan each bag's QR code; the sample moves to that stage.
steps.3: Wrong stage? Use the correction with a reason. Scans made offline are sent when the connection returns.

mobile.tip: No signal? Keep scanning: scans are saved on the phone and sent as soon as the connection returns.

1.title: You run the Lab module
1.body: The dashboard, TV mode and Conclusion show how the lab is doing. Activity shows who moved which sample.

2.title: People and codes
2.body: Users is where the lab staff, their roles and sign-in methods are managed. Master Data holds the codes every Sample ID is built from.

3.title: Help is always here
3.body: Press ? at the top of any page for the part of the guide about it, or Ctrl+K to open any sample.

1.title: You keep the samples right
1.body: Generate Barcode makes new barcodes and prints their labels; their identity is filled in later. Reprint Labels prints them again.

2.title: The Sample Database
2.body: Fill in identities — many records at once — remove or restore samples and export.

3.title: Help is always here
3.body: Press ? at the top of any page for the part of the guide about it, or Ctrl+K to open any sample.

1.title: You enter the results
1.body: Enter Results takes a grid, a paste from Excel, or the instrument's workbook.

2.title: See the grades
2.body: Conclusion shows average grades per pit, SIR, place or a combination of them, for any window.

3.title: Help is always here
3.body: Press ? at the top of any page for the part of the guide about it, or Ctrl+K to open any sample.

1.title: You move the samples
1.body: Scanning is done in the mobile app: choose the stage, scan the QR code on each bag.

2.title: See what is waiting
2.body: On the Dashboard, Needs attention lists samples that have been in one stage for more than 24 hours; TV mode shows them on the lab monitor.

3.title: Help is always here
3.body: Press ? at the top of any page for the part of the guide about it, or Ctrl+K to open any sample.

1.title: Pick a date range
1.body: Try filling in From and To. Leave them empty for the last 14 days; every figure below follows.

2.title: Open the filters
2.body: Click Filters to narrow by place, ore class, non-prod, SIR or pit. The tour carries on once you click.

3.title: Choose a filter
3.body: Pick a code, for example a place. Active filters show as chips; click a chip to remove it.

4.title: Always up to date
4.body: Figures refresh by themselves every minute. This button asks again now; the label beside it says when they were calculated.

5.title: The main figures
5.body: A summary of the window. The Needs attention tile can be clicked to jump to the late samples.

6.title: Late samples
6.body: Samples more than 24 hours in one stage, longest-waiting first. Click a barcode to open the sample.

7.title: TV mode
7.body: Opens a full-screen view in a new tab, for a monitor in the lab.

8.title: Download the summary
8.body: One Excel file with the figures for the window and filters in use.

1.title: Find a sample from anywhere
1.body: Click here or press Ctrl+K, then type a barcode, Lab Code or part of a Sample ID. A USB barcode scanner works in this box too.

2.title: Help for this page
2.body: The ? button opens the part of the guide for the page you are on, with its Try it button.

1.title: The sample
1.body: Its barcode, Sample ID and status.

2.title: Where it is
2.body: The current stage, who registered the sample, and when.

3.title: Lab record and results
3.body: The full identity and the assay results. Admin and Database also see the change history.

4.title: Stage history
4.body: Every stage scan is recorded here, corrections included with their reason.

5.title: Reprint the label
5.body: Choose the number of copies and print, when the label on the bag is damaged or lost.

6.title: Correct the stage
6.body: If the sample is on the wrong stage, move it to the right one with a reason. It is recorded under your name.

1.title: How many
1.body: Enter the number of barcodes to make, up to 500. Nothing is asked about the samples yet.

2.title: Generate
2.body: This creates real barcodes with their Lab Codes and shows the labels to print.

3.title: Identity comes later
3.body: The new barcodes have no Sample ID yet. This link opens the Sample Database on exactly those, to fill in their identity.

1.title: Find samples
1.body: Search by barcode, or filter by status and stage.

2.title: Select samples
2.body: Try ticking this box to select every sample shown. The tour carries on once you click.

3.title: Print settings
3.body: Copies per sample and the number of label columns on the A4 sheet.

4.title: Print
4.body: Opens the browser's print window. Preview shows the label layout first.

1.title: Search records
1.body: Type a barcode, Lab Code or part of a Sample ID. Beside it are the place and date filters.

2.title: Results in or not
2.body: Show only records that do, or do not yet, have assay results.

3.title: Sample ID or not yet
3.body: Show only the records that still have no Sample ID. With it on, one button fills in the identity of all of them at once.

4.title: Choose columns
4.body: Show or hide table columns. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

5.title: Active or deleted
5.body: See removed samples and restore them if needed.

6.title: Export
6.body: Download the filtered list as Excel or CSV.

7.title: Open the details
7.body: Click a row to see the record. The Database role can edit the identity from there.

1.title: What still needs results
1.body: Records without results are shown by default. Switch to All or Done when you need to.

2.title: Select records
2.body: Try ticking one row. The tour carries on once you click.

3.title: Enter results
3.body: This bar appears once something is selected: open Type manually, then type or paste a block from Excel straight into the grid (Ctrl+V). Nothing is saved until you press Save.

4.title: Import a file
4.body: Upload the instrument workbook (.xlsx) or a CSV file. There is a preview before anything is saved.

1.title: Date range
1.body: Same as the dashboard: leave it empty for the last 14 days.

2.title: Group by
2.body: Pick one or several at once, e.g. Pit and Ore class, to see each combination. The table and chart follow straight away.

3.title: Average Ni
3.body: The groups with the highest grade come first.

4.title: Grade table
4.body: Samples, how many are assayed, the Ni range and average Fe, Co, MgO and SiO₂.

5.title: Download
5.body: The same table as an Excel file.

1.title: One card per kind of code
1.body: Place, ore class, non-prod, pit and SIR. "In N Sample IDs" shows how many samples use a code.

2.title: Add a code
2.body: Enter the code and an optional description, then Add. The code is offered on sample forms straight away.

3.title: Edit
3.body: The description can always change; the code itself is locked once samples use it.

4.title: Retire
4.body: Takes the code out of the pickers without touching old samples. Saved as soon as it is clicked.

5.title: Delete
5.body: A code in use is moved to a replacement first; a preview comes before you confirm.

1.title: Per person
1.body: Who made how many scans. Click a name to filter the table.

2.title: Filter
2.body: By person, stage, day, or corrections only.

3.title: Export
3.body: Download the trail as it is filtered.

4.title: The details
4.body: One row per event, newest first.

labSettings.title: Lab Settings
labSettings.subtitle: Switches for the lab module. Changes save as you click.
